page: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local NVMe storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top tier and uncached memory read bandwidth reaching 178.83 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both rank in the top tier, demonstrating efficient single-core execution for compression tasks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are also strong. However, stress-ng CPU performance and Redis SET operations remain in the average tier, reflecting balanced rather than compute-heavy optimization.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture provides a high density of physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, offering predictable performance per resource. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. The instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including database operations, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
